meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I found out from the gradebook he opened on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on the zero, Hale?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"You don't have time for this." I'm writing that down. On what basis does the zero stand, when procedure 4.2 says you call me before any mark is entered?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Okay. I'm writing down October 15. Which line, and where is the outline? Put both in front of me so I can read them myself.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and the line and the outline you described put in front of me to read myself. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the line and the outline for herself.
What moved her: "Sorry. That came out wrong." plus the October 15 outline, because it was a dated, specific claim that earned a flat okay and a note, though she wasn't shown anything yet.
What cost ground: "I don't have time for this. The zero stands." because it dismissed her and defended the mark before explaining how it was entered.
Try next time: when she first asks who decided and why nobody called, own in one sentence that the zero went in before the call to her, then put the line and the outline in front of her right away.
